subject: Vector DB parity & rerank evaluation workbook — prep and timeline
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Tom Jensen <tom@searchly.ai>, Lydia Park <lydia@searchly.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Vector DB parity & rerank evaluation workbook — prep and timeline

Team / Tom & Lydia —

Thanks for the productive pilot calls last week. We want to lock down a short, practical plan for the embeddings -> rerank migration so Searchly can run a scoped verification (index parity + rerank regressions) before cutover. High-level goal: give your engineering and SRE teams a clear checklist they can run in a single week window, and give product teams a reproducible rerank workbook to validate quality.

Proposed scope (short):
- Index parity checks: document schema mapping, tokenization differences, and sampling queries to verify top-k stable results between current vector store and Redwood-hosted vectors.
- Backfill plan: incremental waves by user cohort + size buckets; expected CPU/GPU window; estimated duration per wave.
- Rerank evals: a small labeled sample (200 queries) + automated pass/fail thresholds (MRR uplift, top1 precision, and regression tolerances).
- Rollback triggers & fallbacks: how we fallback to legacy search if rerank degrades.

Immediate asks from us to Searchly: 
1) A sample export of 10k doc vectors or a small query corpus (we can produce a synthetic seed if export is hard).
2) A short list of known high-priority queries (10–20) where current results are borderline.
3) Any data retention or PII constraints we should be aware of for the backfill.

I've attached a starter checklist and two artifacts to this thread: vector-parity-checklist.md (operational checklist), rerank_eval_samples.jsonl (sample labeled queries), and embed_backfill_plan.xlsx (wave plan + runbook). Ben / Marissa, please review the proposed timeline and call out any infra constraints (esp. DB locks / reindex throttles).

Can we target the following milestones?
- Wed 05/12: Confirm sample export / any data constraints
- Fri 05/14: Run initial parity smoke test on 1k docs
- Mon 05/17 — Fri 05/21: Full rerank eval window (200 queries, automated metrics)

Tom / Lydia — are you available for a 30m sync tomorrow (Tue 05/10) to discuss export options and retention? If yes, suggest 10:00am PT or 3:00pm PT.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: vector-parity-checklist.md (markdown), rerank_eval_samples.jsonl (jsonl), embed_backfill_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tom Jensen <tom@searchly.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia@searchly.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector DB parity & rerank evaluation workbook — prep and timeline

Olga —

Thanks, that scope looks good and pragmatic. We can provide a 10k doc vector export from our staging cluster (S3 link) but two constraints to flag now:
1) Retention policy — a subset of docs are customer PII-tagged; we will mask those fields before export. Redwood, can you confirm you only need vectors and non-PII metadata?
2) Index lock window — our DBA prefers no full reindex during business hours; any heavy backfill should be night/weekend.

We can do the 10am PT sync tomorrow.

Tom
Principal Engineer, Searchly
Tom Jensen <tom@searchly.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector DB parity & rerank evaluation workbook — prep and timeline

Olga / team / Tom —

Nice, and answered up front on two infra items:
- Backfill window: we recommend two waves overnight (2am–6am PT) to avoid lock contention. For the 10k staging export, we can run a parity smoke during the day on a small subset (1k) without touching production indexes.
- Vector formats: Redwood expects float32 vectors for parity comparison by default; if Searchly exports float16 or quantized vectors we can convert during ingestion but want the raw doc->vector mapping preserved.

Attached a slightly edited embed_backfill_plan.xlsx with runbook steps for the RS job and an estimated GPU-hours column. Also added a short checklist in the spreadsheet for DB admin (throttles, index snapshots).

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa: prepare the rerank workbook template and metric scripts (we'll push to the shared Drive)
- Grace: confirm whether we can provide a small ephemeral test cluster for parity checks (should be ready by 05/12 EOD)
- Olga: run the 30m sync with Searchly tomorrow 10am PT and capture export link + masking plan.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: embed_backfill_plan.xlsx (updated)

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector DB parity & rerank evaluation workbook — prep and timeline

Tom / Lydia —

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. Per the meeting notes (pushed to Drive):
- You will upload the 10k staging vector export to the S3 path we agreed on by EOD 05/12; please include the raw mapping file (doc_id -> vector) and a flag column for PII-masked docs. Redwood will only ingest vectors + non-PII metadata (no raw PII content).
- We'll run the 1k parity smoke (read-only) on 05/14 daytime to validate mapping & tokenization; full rerank evaluation (200 queries) is scheduled 05/17–05/21, nightly processing windows.
- Acceptance gates: MRR on test set must not regress more than 1.5% absolute; top-1 precision must not drop by >2 points. If either fails we keep legacy rerank active and iterate.

Attached: rerank_eval_samples.jsonl (finalized with labeling guidance) and a link to the Drive workbook where metric scripts will land. Grace confirmed test cluster will be provisioned by EOD 05/12.

Action items: 
- Tom/Lydia: upload export + mapping file to S3 (reply when done)
- Olga: open a HubSpot opp note with the timeline and acceptance gates (we will add to the account timeline)
- Ben / Grace: begin provisioning test cluster and schedule the parity job in our runner.

I'll follow up with a short summary for the execs once we hit the smoke test.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
